content:
A single point cannot cover all of \(S\): in any \(2\times2\) block, one corner has the same parity as that point, so both coordinate differences are even, giving \(\gcd\ge 2\).

Now take
\[
T=\{(3,2),(2,3)\}.
\]
Let \(A=(3,2)\), \(B=(2,3)\).

- For rows \(b=1,3\), the vertical distance from \(A\) is \(1\), so every point in those rows is visible from \(A\).
- For rows \(b=2,4\), the vertical distance from \(B\) is \(1\), so every point in those rows is visible from \(B\).
- For row \(b=5\):
  \[
  (1,5),(2,5),(4,5),(5,5)
  \]
  are visible from \(A\), since \(\gcd(|a-3|,3)=1\), and
  \[
  (3,5)
  \]
  is visible from \(B\), since \((3-2,5-3)=(1,2)\).

Thus two points suffice, and one cannot suffice.

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
